property_summary: Only the current owner can change the owner via transferOwnership; the buggy modifier removes this check, so any non-owner caller can also change it.

After any sequence of transferOwnership calls by any callers, the owner must be among the addresses that successfully invoked transferOwnership (allowing only the current owner to change it). The buggy version violates this because any caller can become owner.
For any initial owner and any new owner, after a transferOwnership call by a non-owner, the owner remains unchanged in the reference but can change in the buggy version.
After any call to transferOwnership with any address, the owner must equal the newOwner argument in the correct contract, but the buggy contract always sets owner to a fixed address.

After two successive transferOwnership calls by the owner with distinct newOwner addresses A and B, owner() must equal B in the correct contract, but the buggy contract sets owner to the fixed address after the first call and never changes it again, so the second call leaves owner at the fixed address.

After the owner calls transferOwnership with any newOwner address, the correct contract updates owner to that address, but the buggy contract sets owner to a fixed address instead, so the resulting owner differs for any newOwner not equal to that fixed address.

For any initial owner, after two consecutive transferOwnership calls by the owner with arbitrary addresses X and Y, the final owner must equal Y in the correct contract, but the bug sets owner to a fixed address on the first call and never changes it again.
After the owner calls transferOwnership with any newOwner, the owner must equal newOwner, but the bug sets it to a fixed address instead.
After any call to transferOwnership, the owner becomes the newOwner parameter; the bug breaks this by setting owner to msg.sender instead.
After transferOwnership is called by the current owner, the owner should always remain the current owner; the bug incorrectly changes owner to msg.sender.
After any transferOwnership call, the owner must equal the newOwner argument, but the buggy version breaks this by resetting owner to address(this).
After any call to transferOwnership(newOwner) by the current owner, the owner variable must equal newOwner; the mutant violates this by not updating owner.
For any allowed call to transferOwnership by an owner, the owner address after the call must equal the newOwner address; the mutant leaves owner unchanged.

If the owner is NOT the zero address and a call to transferOwnership by the current owner succeeds (no revert), then the new owner after the call must equal the newOwner argument; the mutant leaves owner unchanged.

For any call to transferOwnership by the current owner, the owner remains the same after the call if and only if the caller is not the current owner; the buggy version always leaves owner unchanged even when the caller is the owner, so a call by the owner does not change owner.
A successful call to owned() from the owner never reverts on the correct contract, but always reverts on the buggy contract.
The owner can always successfully call owned() without reverting; the buggy version selfdestructs, destroying the contract and making future calls or balance checks fail.
For any caller, after a successful call to owned(), the contract c must still exist (i.e., address(c).code.length > 0); the buggy version selfdestructs, destroying the contract.
For any address that is the owner, a call to owned() does not revert; the buggy version always reverts due to selfdestruct halting execution.
For any successful call to owned() by the owner, the contract must still exist afterwards; the buggy version selfdestructs and destroys the contract.
For any owner call to owned(), the contract must still be alive (code size > 0) after the call; the buggy version selfdestructs and destroys the contract.
For the reference contract, a call to owned() from any non-owner address always reverts; the buggy modifier removes the require, so a non-owner call succeeds, changing the revert behavior.
A successful call to owned() must succeed and not revert, but the buggy version always reverts because the condition is hard-coded to false, making any call to owned() fail.
A caller that is the current owner can successfully call owned() without revert, but the buggy modifier makes every call revert regardless of caller.
caller == owner must be able to successfully call owned, but the bug negates the condition so the owner cannot call it

After deploy, any address can become owner in the buggy version, while in the reference only the current owner can transfer ownership: calling transferOwnership from a non-owner should never change the owner from the pre-call owner.

In the reference contract, the owner can only be changed by the current owner calling transferOwnership; the bug allows any account to change the owner, so the owner after a non-owner call must remain unchanged in P but may change in M.
After any call to transferOwnership by the current owner, the owner state variable should be updated to the argument passed; the bug assigns the argument to itself, leaving owner unchanged.

After a call to transferOwnership by the owner, the owner state variable must equal the argument; the bug performs a self-assignment on the argument instead of updating owner, so owner stays unchanged.

For any caller, the owner after transferOwnership(newOwner) must equal the newOwner if the caller is the current owner, but the buggy modifier instead allows transfer only when the caller is NOT the owner, causing the owner to remain unchanged for the legitimate owner and change for any non-owner.
For the current owner, transferOwnership(newOwner) must update owner to newOwner; with the inverted guard the call reverts and owner stays unchanged.

For any caller, if the caller is the current owner, transferOwnership(newOwner) must succeed and set owner to newOwner; the buggy version reverts for the owner but succeeds for a non-owner, leaving owner unchanged.
